topics.title: Kira Labs
topics.label: Independent research & creation
topics.answer: Kira Labs is Robert McMurrer’s independent research and creation studio. Kira World is its central project. Related work includes Sarah Travel and a local Video Studio. The aim is useful software with continuity and personal control, developed through prototypes and testing. Current prototypes also explore staffing, decision evidence, task readiness and simpler browser media planning.

topics.title: Kira World
topics.label: Working prototypes + ongoing research
topics.answer: Kira World explores distinct synthetic people whose identity, reviewed memories and voice can continue between sessions. Local conversation experiments and a basic walkable Home World exist. A polished shared 3D world, believable bodies and clothing, VR and compatible embodiment remain development goals. It is experimental software, not a finished public product.

details.answer: Kira World connects three ideas: distinct people, continuity between conversations, and places in which to spend time. Home World is the continuing home, while future Notebook Worlds provide settings for activities. VR and compatible robotics are longer-term interfaces. Local conversation and continuity experiments and a basic apartment exist; that combination is not yet a finished shared world.

how.answer:
Kira World is being built around separate responsibilities. The conversation model supplies dialogue: an August 10, 2026 roadmap selected qwen3.5:9b for normal Kira text conversation, but the model running today has not been verified. Per-person identity identifies who is speaking, while retained, reviewed memory provides context from earlier interactions. Local identity and continuity experiments exist.

Runtime events and world state are separate from dialogue. The public design also separates permissioned actions; saying that something happened is not proof of a completed world action, and a generated statement does not automatically become a saved memory. Voice is another responsibility, with local speech and voice-reference experiments. The visible body and world provide presence: a basic walkable Home World shell exists, while believable bodies and clothing remain unfinished work.

This describes documented responsibilities, existing experiments and intended connections. It is not a claim that every part already works together as a finished resident or shared world. The reviewed notes do not establish a complete current model count, database design or implementation algorithm.
how.label: Documented components · prototypes and plans

privacy.answer: The stated direction favors local control of personal state and permission for external actions. It does not establish that every future voice, device or world feature is offline, or supply a complete retention and sharing policy.

status.answer: Local conversation, person-specific continuity and speech experiments exist, along with a basic walkable apartment. Complete populated worlds, accessible VR and compatible physical embodiment remain goals. There is no confirmed public launch date for the full experience.

components.answer: Kira World has several connected parts, at different stages. Minds are the distinct people: local identity, reviewed-memory and voice experiments support continuing conversations. Home World is their intended home; a basic walkable one-bedroom shell exists. Notebook Worlds are future settings for study, travel, creativity, history and play. Temporary Creator designs people for particular worlds or activities; public spoken tests exist, with factual errors and unfinished avatars or bodies still visible. VR is a future way to share those places, with no confirmed headset release. Robotics is a longer-term, simulation-first route to compatible physical embodiment—not a deployed autonomous robot. The work is to connect these foundations into a continuing shared experience.

topics.title: Memory & identity
topics.label: Person-specific continuity
topics.answer: Kira World’s approach keeps person-specific identity and reviewed memory records separate from the immediate conversation. The aim is for Kira, Lisa and future residents to remain distinct and continue across sessions. Local continuity experiments exist; that does not yet establish a complete persistent life across every device or world.

details.answer: A person’s identity provides a continuing reference for who is speaking; reviewed memory supplies context from earlier interactions. Keeping those records separate from the immediate conversation is intended to help Kira and Lisa remain distinct across sessions. It does not establish a complete life across every world or device.

how.answer:
Identity and memory have different jobs. A per-person identity keeps the reference to who Kira or Lisa is; retained, reviewed memory supplies context from earlier interactions, separate from the immediate conversation. The July 23 public update distinguishes spoken dialogue, private thoughts, runtime events and reviewed memory. A model reply is not automatically a saved memory or proof that an action happened.

These memory responsibilities sit alongside conversation, world state and permissioned actions, with voice and the visible body serving different roles. Local identity and continuity experiments exist; continuity across every world or device remains a goal. The dated August 10 roadmap selected qwen3.5:9b for text conversation, not a verified complete memory architecture or current running-model inventory. The reviewed notes do not specify a database engine, memory-search algorithm or complete storage schema.

status.answer: Local continuity experiments exist. A complete persistent identity working across every device and world has not been established by these notes.

topics.answer: This website’s Sarah answers in your browser from a small set of published notes. Your questions are not sent to an AI provider or emailed to Robert. topics.title: Sarah on this website
topics.label: Text conversation · no setup
topics.answer: I’m Sarah, the Kira Labs website guide. I answer from these dated project notes and can help with Robert’s work and a short factual bio. Click Voice on once to hear the current answer and following replies until you choose Voice off or leave the page. It uses an available browser/device voice, not a custom clone, and does not request your microphone. The text guide needs no account, API key, installed model or credits.
next: Write a mini bio of Robert

details.answer: This website guide retrieves answers from its dated knowledge file. It can remember the current topic during this visit and use separate notes for follow-up questions. It is not running Robert’s private Kira World residents or their memories.

how.answer: This page matches questions to dated topics and follow-up notes in the browser. Voice on enables browser/device read-aloud for the current and following answers until you turn it off or leave. It does not request microphone access, and this website is not running Robert’s private resident voice system.

privacy.answer: Text questions stay in this page’s conversation memory until you reload or clear it; they are not emailed to Robert or sent to an AI provider for generated answers. The page does not request a microphone. Read-aloud uses browser/device speech, whose service behavior can vary, so an offline guarantee is not claimed.

status.answer: The text guide is available here. One click on Voice on reads the current and following replies when browser/device speech is supported, until Voice off or leaving the page. No microphone or custom voice clone is used.

cost.answer: The website text guide requires no account, API key, installed model or usage credits. It retrieves these notes in the browser.

voice.answer: Choose Voice on once to read the current answer aloud and keep reading following replies. Voice off stops it, and leaving the page stops speech. Availability depends on your browser and device voices. No microphone is requested and no custom voice clone is claimed.

details.answer: Home World supplies the continuing-home part of the vision: a place to return to between conversations and activities. Notebook Worlds are proposed other settings for particular purposes. The apartment shell demonstrates a basic walkable space, not completed residents, physical interactions or autonomous daily routines.

how.answer: The existing evidence is a basic walkable apartment. The intended connection to person-specific identity and memory is broader than that space. These notes do not document a completed system that gives residents ongoing daily lives there.

topics.title: CutBrief
topics.label: Submitted prototype · public workspace · September 8, 2026
topics.answer: CutBrief helps turn a video idea into an editable shot plan, with actor and location references, saved takes, trimming, captions and stitched landscape, vertical and square exports. It supports business updates, tutorials, travel, family and social videos. The tested free workflow uses your supplied media and written planning; it needs no paid generation credits. Appearance references remain separate from opening frames. A composed-scene review path is prepared, but paid scene and video generation are locked pending owner review. No successful hosted generation or finished automatic movie workflow is claimed. Robert reports that CutBrief has been submitted, and its approved public workspace link is now available below. This does not establish a contest result or unlock paid generation.

Appearance references remain separate from opening frames. A composed-scene review path is prepared, but paid scene and video generation remain locked pending owner review.

how.answer: Start from a video idea and written shot plan, add your own media and references, then review takes, timing, captions and the assembled result. The tested free path uses supplied media and written planning. It is not evidence that a hosted generator can automatically film an entire movie.

status.answer: Robert reports that CutBrief has been submitted. The approved public workspace is linked below. This supersedes the older note saying no public access link was announced. Paid generation remains locked; submission is not a claim of a contest result.

privacy.answer: The available CutBrief notes do not establish a complete policy for uploaded-media retention or sharing. A public workspace link is not a privacy guarantee. Check the workspace’s current information before supplying sensitive material.

limits.answer: A public submitted prototype is available, but paid scene/video generation stays locked. Neither successful hosted generation nor a finished automatic movie workflow is claimed.

topics.title: ShiftBrief
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: ShiftBrief is a team-planning desk for stores, offices and other teams. It records employee availability, opening hours and staffing needs, then proposes a week for review. Coverage displays, lunch choices, sick-call replacement options and dated history use the saved team facts. Accepting a reviewed proposal saves it; asking does not contact anyone or claim a replacement agreed to work. Source notes and cited handoffs remain available. The standard written Sarah workflow is a bounded planner, with no model, API key or usage credits required. Its no-install browser prototype is in private owner review. It is not a payroll system, labor-law assessment or public released service.

topics.title: ClearTrail
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: ClearTrail helps office, home, research and community projects keep evidence behind a decision. Import text or readable PDFs, retain revisions, compare exact changes and ask Sarah for matching source passages. Saved briefings keep their quotes and can be exported; older briefings are marked when the evidence changes. Possible disagreements remain for review, and a newer record is not automatically approved. The default written workflow is bounded retrieval and comparison, not a general language model. The browser prototype requires no installed model, API key or credits and remains in private owner review. It is not connected to an Alexa device and has no announced public access link.

topics.title: Carry On
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: Carry On organizes work, home, travel and other plans into tasks, dependencies and readiness checks. Written Sarah can help develop a plan and propose changes; reviewed confirmations apply supported changes while preserving task IDs and history. Dependency cycles and stale edits are rejected. The browser prototype saves work in this browser and supports real export, backup and restore. Its bounded planning core needs no installed model, API key, voice folder or usage credits. It is in private owner review, with no public judge-access link announced. Carry On does not book travel, send messages or run a connected Alexa assistant.

topics.title: Kira Sequence Desk
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: Kira Sequence Desk is the smaller browser sequence-planning prototype for the AI Builders work. Turn your notes into timed, source-linked steps; revise wording, order and timing; attach your own images, audio or video; and review coverage gaps. Written approval applies to the exact plan and clears after edits. Export produces an editable ZIP with the plan, source map, review issues and selected original media. It does not render a finished movie or generate new footage. Written Sarah uses a bounded source planner, not a general language model, and requires no model, API key, account or voice installation. Work stays in browser storage with backup and restore. This is in private owner review, separate from the full personal Video Studio, with no public access link announced.

topics.title: Minds & distinct residents
topics.label: Kira World · published direction and current evidence
topics.answer: In Kira World, a “mind” means the software behind a distinct synthetic person. Kira and Lisa are intended to have their own identity, history, reviewed memories and voice, so a later conversation can continue with the same person. Local conversation and continuity experiments exist. This is not a claim that the software is conscious or has verified feelings.

details.answer: The aim is continuity with an individual, rather than a new interchangeable character every time. Identity describes who the resident is; history and reviewed memories provide context from earlier interactions; a distinct voice helps preserve that identity in conversation. Kira and Lisa are separate residents in that design. The intended connection to Home World would give those continuing interactions a place, while future Notebook Worlds would provide other settings and activities. Local experiments support parts of this direction, but they do not establish a fully independent life across every world or device. “Mind” is a plain-language description here, not a scientific finding of consciousness.

how.answer: The published approach separates a person’s identity and reviewed memory records from the immediate conversation. A later session can use that retained context to support continuity while keeping different people’s histories distinct. That explains the intended role of memory; the available public notes do not specify a complete mind architecture, exact model count or algorithm. Generated language about emotions is not, by itself, proof of a lived experience.

privacy.answer: For residents, the stated direction is local control of personal state and reviewed memory, with permission for external actions. That is a design principle, not a verified guarantee that every future voice, world or device feature stays offline. These public notes do not establish a complete retention, deletion or device-sync policy for residents. This website guide is separate from Robert’s private resident histories.

status.answer: Local person-specific conversation, identity, reviewed-memory continuity and speech experiments exist. The evidence does not establish finished persistent residents living independently in a shared 3D world, or one complete identity working across all devices. There is no confirmed public launch date for that full experience.

voice.answer: A distinct voice is part of the intended identity of each resident, and local speech experiments exist. That is separate from the browser voice reading this website’s answers. The public notes do not establish a finished voice that follows each resident through every world and device.

limits.answer: Separate identity records and convincing conversation do not prove consciousness, verified feelings or autonomous daily life. The current evidence supports bounded prototypes. A fully populated persistent world and cross-device embodiment remain goals.

technical.answer: An August 10, 2026 technical roadmap selected qwen3.5:9b for normal Kira text conversation. That is a dated selection; the model currently running has not been verified. The reviewed public material does not establish the exact models currently powering Kira World residents, their count, or which are running at once. It describes identity, reviewed memory, voice and world responsibilities. Production Director’s published Gemini defaults belong to a separate cloud demo, so they should not be substituted for a resident model list.

topics.title: Notebook Worlds
topics.label: Kira World · published direction and current evidence
topics.answer: Notebook Worlds are proposed places within Kira World for particular activities: travel, learning, creative work, history and play. Home World is the continuing home; a Notebook World provides another setting for an activity. The aim is to retain the same people and continuity between places. Complete populated Notebook Worlds are a future goal, not a finished feature shown by the current apartment prototype.

details.answer: The distinction is purpose. Home World provides a continuing home, while a Notebook World can focus on an activity or subject. The public examples include travel, study, creativity, history and play. The longer-term idea is that entering another setting would not mean abandoning the identity and history developed at home. That could make separate activities part of one continuing experience. Those examples describe the intended use, not a catalogue of worlds you can enter today. The present visible evidence is a basic walkable one-bedroom Home World shell.

how.answer: Conceptually, a Notebook World gives an activity its own place while drawing on continuity with Home World. The public notes describe that relationship, but do not establish the implementation of world creation, transitions, shared sessions or memory exchange. I should not turn the concept into a claim that a working world generator or portal system is already available.

privacy.answer: Continuity between places raises questions about which personal history accompanies a resident and who can access it. Local control and permission are the broader stated direction. The reviewed public notes do not yet define Notebook World-specific sharing, retention or access rules, so I cannot promise that all future worlds are private or offline.

status.answer: Notebook Worlds remain future development. The basic walkable apartment is Home World evidence; it is not evidence that populated travel, study or historical worlds have been completed. No public Notebook World access link or release date is confirmed.

voice.answer: The intended continuity includes the same resident identity and voice across activities and places. Local voice experiments do not prove that this already works inside completed Notebook Worlds.

limits.answer: The listed activities are examples of the vision. They do not establish completed world libraries, live multiplayer, automatic world generation or historically accurate simulations.

topics.title: Temporary Creator
topics.label: Public development tests · July 24–25, 2026
topics.answer: Temporary Creator, called TemporaryAI Creator in Robert’s public videos, is being developed to create synthetic people for particular worlds or activities. The aim is a coherent identity, knowledge, personality, appearance and voice. Public July 24–25 development videos describe actual voice-conversation tests, including mistakes and unfinished avatars or bodies. That is more than a written concept, but not a completed animated resident.

details.answer: The concept begins with a person’s purpose, identity, knowledge limits and personality, with appearance and voice belonging to the same design. Robert’s July 24 explainer describes creation types, source packs, historical dates and life stages, avatar references and voice evidence. The following public tests report both usable conversation and failures: invented details, internal system language appearing in speech, and claims of saved work that were not true. Some tests use individual test voices; others use generic Windows voices. These are development demonstrations, not a finished complete-person system. Temporary people are not automatically permanent Home World residents, and the name does not promise deletion when a chat closes.

how.answer: The public explainer describes choosing a creation type, preparing sources, setting the relevant date or life stage, considering avatar references and evaluating voice evidence. Its proposed connection reaches world placement and Video Studio. The companion tests report voice conversations with concrete failures and unfinished avatars or bodies, so those described connections should not all be treated as completed. Historical variants are synthetic interpretations, not the literal people; voice and reference material still require appropriate evidence and authorization.

privacy.answer: The name does not define a data-retention policy. The public explainer discusses authenticity, rights and authorization for source and voice material, but these notes do not establish a complete retention, deletion or sharing policy. I cannot promise that a temporary person is deleted after an interaction. The explanations here use public descriptions and general owner concepts, not private memories or person designs.

status.answer: Public development videos published July 24–25, 2026 report actual TemporaryAI voice-conversation tests. They also document factual errors, incorrect saved-work claims, generic voice fallbacks and unfinished avatars or bodies. The dated videos establish demonstrated experiments, not today’s live runtime state or a completed animated person living in a world. No general public application release or completion date is confirmed here.

voice.answer: Voice conversations appear in the public development tests. Some descriptions identify individualized test voices; others explicitly identify generic Windows voices while individual voices remain unfinished. These tests do not establish a finished body-and-voice creation pipeline. Historical or fictional test voices are not automatically authentic recordings or official performances.

limits.answer: The public tests retain failures instead of presenting every answer as fact: they report invented details, internal language leaking into dialogue and incorrect claims that files were saved. Avatars, bodies and individual voices remain unfinished in the described tests. A demonstrated conversation is not proof of a complete animated resident or reliable research and file operations.

topics.title: Virtual reality
topics.label: Kira World · published direction and current evidence
topics.answer: Virtual reality is a future way of sharing Kira World’s places with its residents. The ambition is accessible, multimodal presence while keeping the same identity and history across devices and worlds. The current public evidence does not establish a finished VR release, supported headset list or launch date.

details.answer: The aspiration is presence in the same digital places, rather than losing the relationship and history whenever the interface changes. Accessibility and different ways of interacting are part of that direction. Home World and future Notebook Worlds give context to the idea. The polished world illustrations are concept art; they are not proof of a complete headset experience.

how.answer: The intended connection is between the same resident identity and history and a different way of entering the world. The public notes do not specify completed headset integration, tracking, controls or accessibility features. Those details remain unconfirmed rather than something I can infer from the VR goal.

privacy.answer: VR can involve device-specific tracking and voice services. The public Kira World notes do not define those future data flows or permissions. Local control is a design preference, not a promise that an unspecified headset or speech service keeps every signal on the device.

status.answer: VR remains a future direction. A basic walkable Home World exists, but these notes do not establish a publicly available VR product, supported headset or release date.

limits.answer: There is no confirmed device compatibility list, controller scheme, tracking specification or finished shared VR world in the reviewed notes.

topics.title: Robotics & physical embodiment
topics.label: Kira World · published direction and current evidence
topics.answer: Compatible physical embodiment is a longer-term Kira World goal: exploring whether a continuing identity could interact through suitable robotic hardware. The stated direction is simulation first, followed by controlled tests. The public evidence does not establish a deployed autonomous robot.

details.answer: The connection to Kira World is continuity: a resident should not become an unrelated identity simply because the interface changes from a screen or virtual place to compatible hardware. This is an aspiration for future embodiment. Simulation and controlled testing come before a claim of physical capability. It does not mean Kira or Lisa currently has an operating robot body.

how.answer: The published direction begins in simulation and proceeds through controlled tests of compatible embodiment. The reviewed notes do not identify a completed hardware integration, robot model, movement controller or autonomous task capability. I can explain the goal, but not provide a verified operating procedure for a robot that has not been established here.

privacy.answer: Physical embodiment would introduce questions about sensors, recordings and permission for actions. The public notes do not establish a robot-specific data or access policy. The general preference for local control should not be read as a guarantee about unchosen hardware or future services.

status.answer: Robotics is a longer-term goal, with simulation-first work as the stated approach. No deployed autonomous robot, supported hardware list or delivery date is confirmed by these public notes.

limits.answer: A software identity or simulation is not evidence of a safe, capable physical robot. These notes do not verify autonomous real-world movement, household tasks or sensor access.

topics.title: Avatar bodies & clothing
topics.answer: Avatar bodies and clothing are active development work. Public notes describe articulated test foundations, and the TemporaryAI Creator explainer includes appearance references and an intended Avatar Builder step. The July conversation tests still had unfinished individual bodies or avatars. A believable, fully animated resident with finished clothing behavior is not established by those demonstrations.

status.answer: Public notes document body and garment test foundations. The July 24–25 TemporaryAI descriptions still report unfinished avatars or individual bodies. Those are development results, not a finished animated-resident release.

how.answer: The public TemporaryAI explainer describes appearance references and an Avatar Builder step as part of the intended creation workflow. Separate body work calls for articulated non-person fixtures before believable garment behavior is claimed. It does not publish a complete verified body-building procedure.

technical.answer: The reviewed public material does not establish a complete current avatar engine, rig specification or clothing-simulation stack. I can explain the described test goals without inventing those implementation details.

topics.title: World Builder & future places
topics.answer: World Builder is a proposed direction for creating places, with Home World and future Notebook Worlds providing the context. The public evidence supports a basic walkable apartment shell; it does not yet establish a working general world editor or a verified creation procedure. Robert is also considering a museum experience for Meta as a future commercial idea. That is a new owner proposal, not a finished Meta application or a revenue claim.

status.answer: A basic walkable Home World shell is documented. A general World Builder, its tools and creation steps are not yet established by the reviewed public evidence. The museum direction is a proposal, with no finished Meta app or launch date.

how.answer: The published idea is to have a continuing Home World and purpose-built Notebook Worlds for activities. I do not have a verified World Builder procedure, template list or file-format specification to walk you through.

cost.answer: Robert’s newly stated proposal is to explore a museum experience for Meta as a possible commercial direction. The format, platform support and business model still need definition and testing; these notes establish no finished app, platform agreement, customers or revenue.

technical.answer: No reviewed public source establishes World Builder’s engine, supported formats, generation model or Meta platform compatibility. Those details need a published implementation or supported plan before I can name them.

topics.title: Production Director cloud demo
topics.answer: Production Director is a separate public cloud demo. Its August 31 source describes a structured production brief, planning images and a narrated pitch assembled with FFmpeg. The published defaults name Gemini for planning and images and Google Cloud speech for narration. Those defaults are not a current deployment check or Kira World’s resident model list.

technical.answer: The public cloud-demo source defaults to gemini-3.5-flash for the structured production brief. The August 31 demo description also names Gemini 3.5 Flash. A configurable source default is not a measurement of the model currently serving a deployment. This name must not be described as Kira World’s resident conversation model. In the 2026-08-31 public source, the public cloud-demo source defaults to gemini-3.1-flash-image for storyboard planning images. The deployment can override this default. Planning panels do not establish generated acting or a finished dramatic film. In the 2026-08-31 public source, the public cloud-demo code uses Google Cloud Text-to-Speech Chirp 3 HD for narration and defaults to en-US-Chirp3-HD-Aoede. The configured voice can be changed; current deployed voice was not queried.

how.answer: In the 2026-08-31 public source, the public Production Director code separates an HTTP API, durable jobs, task dispatch, and a private worker. Model responses supply a structured brief and planning images; ordinary code builds storyboard cards, checks coverage, and assembles the narrated pitch with FFmpeg. This is a separate cloud demo, not the local Studio or Kira World resident runtime. Published code and test results alone do not prove a current live deployment completed provider calls.

status.answer: The public repository and August 31 demonstration are dated evidence. No current deployment or provider run was queried for these notes. The cloud demo is separate from local Video Studio and Kira World residents.

topics.title: Local Studio model roles
topics.answer: The September 8 authored technical notes distinguish tested local tools from configured support: PhotoMaker with SDXL generated a portrait; MuseTalk generated a speaking video; Chatterbox speech worked in one test and failed later. VACE, Stable Video Diffusion and ACE-Step have configuration or support evidence here, not a new successful generation claim. These are local Studio roles, separate from Kira residents and the Production Director cloud demo.
